2024_171_m062024bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held June 20, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, record a public hearing on the 2024/2025 proposed budget, recognitions, and a series of unanimous 7-0 votes. The Board adopted a Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage, ratified the successor Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA collective bargaining agreement covering February 1, 2024 through April 15, 2027, and approved two Food Service Fund purchases: serving lines from Stafford-Smith, Inc. for $317,179.00 and three UNOX ovens from Gold Star Products for $90,589.75. Administrative appointments for Trevor Harker and Daniel Trudel took effect July 1, 2024.
2024_171_m062024bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, June 20, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and it adjourned at 8:40 p.m. Minutes were signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education (typist mark GH/jh); the minutes document carries a July 16, 2024 meeting date.

**Attendance**
Present with President Schmidt were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, Pagel, Fulcher, Smotherman, and West. Approximately 60 members of the audience attended.

**Public Hearing — 2024/2025 Proposed Budget**
Mr. West presented the proposed budget with a PowerPoint, covering tax values, homestead/non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund and capital projects fund, student enrollment, foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board noted it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 6th Workshop. President Schmidt invited audience questions; none were asked.

**Recognitions**
- Troy United Synchronized Swim Team, 2024 State Champions, introduced by Mr. Fulcher and presented a team plaque.
- The Business Office team, for the Association of School Business Officials International (ASBO) Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting honoring the Troy School District's Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023. Rick West, Deputy Superintendent, and Kandice Moynihan, former Finance Director, and the Finance team were named.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage**
Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mrs. Anne; adopted 7 yes, 0 no. The resolution directs the Superintendent to periodically communicate the importance of safe firearm storage during gun violence awareness month and to disseminate material annually in the District's annual notification materials, and commits the Board and Superintendent to continued work with local law enforcement, medical and mental health agencies, and non-profits. It states it shall not be construed to conflict with existing Michigan or federal law. Certification cites the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Actions**

| Item | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| Consent agenda items A through I | Hauff / Haupt | 7-0 |
| Trevor Harker, Special Education Supervisor, two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2024 | Alic / Hauff | 7-0 |
| Daniel Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2024 | Philippart / Wilson | 7-0 |
| TEA/MEA/NEA tentative agreement, February 1, 2024 – April 15, 2027 | Anne / Philippart | 7-0 |
| Serving lines, Stafford-Smith, Inc., $317,179.00, Food Service Fund | Philippart / Alic | 7-0 |
| Three UNOX ovens, Gold Star Products, $90,589.75, Food Service Fund | Alic / Haupt | 7-0 |

**Consent Agenda Contents**
Minutes of the May 7, 2024 Special Board meeting; May 7, 2024 Closed Session; May 7, 2024 Board Workshop; May 21, 2024 Board meeting; Treasurer's Report — April 2024; MHSAA Membership Resolution 2024/2025; 2023/2024 Budget Amendment; 2024/2025 Budget Appropriations Resolution; and Approval of Committee for Instructional Minutes.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda)**
Walt Storrs raised flooding and drainage in the Sylvan Glen subdivision tied to construction of the Troy Preschool. Alex Karpowitsch addressed key performance indicators and distributed a Detroit Public Schools "Project 2026 Blueprint" PowerPoint. Tracy Owens addressed special education and said her three children would not attend Troy Schools next year.

**Other**
Dr. Machesky reported Oakland County School Board Association recognitions. Mr. Schmidt discussed graduations and school funding, and announced the next Board meeting for July 16th at Central Office at 9:30 in the morning.
2024_171_m062024bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held June 20, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The minutes bear the title M062024BdMtg and a meeting date of July 16, 2024, the date they were brought forward. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, Pagel, Fulcher, Smotherman, and West. There were approximately 60 members of the audience. The meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the typist notation GH/jh.

**Business — Public Hearing on the 2024/2025 Proposed Budget.** Mr. West presented the details of the proposed budget to the Board and community and shared a PowerPoint presentation. He noted the proposed budget had been reviewed in great detail with the Board at the June workshop. His presentation covered tax values, homestead and non-homestead millage, and general fund adjustments and assumptions. He also spoke about ancillary funds, the sinking fund, and the capital projects fund, and reviewed student enrollment, the District's foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 6th Workshop. President Schmidt invited questions from the audience related to the proposed budget; no questions were asked.

**Recognition — Troy United Synchronized Swim Team, 2024 State Champions.** The Board congratulated the team on a successful season and invited Mr. Fulcher to the podium to introduce the team and present a team plaque. Swim team state champions from Troy High were Rebecca Austin, Erin Choi, Sonia De Donno, Jessica Deng, Ainsley Giorio, Shatakshi Gupta, Ana Sofia Hernandez Gomez, Nidhi Mody, Sei Park, Himasree Puppala, Lucie Rosati, Parker Silagy, Avani Singh, Cate Sivier, Kara Son, Isabel Thommana, Sritha Velireddy, Sasha Vivek, and Sia Wu. Swim team state champions from Athens were Greta Burt, Faith Frederick, Crystal Hensley, McKenzie Johnson, Sakura Mori, and Gwendolyn Schaefer. Coaches Lori Uchwal-Hollier, Erika Mooney, Beth Borland, and Nicole Cervantes were recognized and congratulated for their dedication and hard work.

**Recognition — ASBO Excellence in Financial Reporting for FY2023.** Mr. Schmidt recognized the Business Office team for again receiving the ASBO Award. The Association of School Business Officials International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting Program honored the Troy School District for excellence in the preparation and issuance of a high quality Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023. Named for recognition were Rick West, Deputy Superintendent; Kandice Moynihan, former Finance Director; and the Finance team and staff.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage.** Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne. The whereas clauses state that the safety and well-being of students, teachers, and staff is a top priority in the Troy School District; that firearm-related deaths are the leading cause of death among children and adolescents; that rates of death from firearms among ages 14 to 17 are now 22.5% higher than motor vehicle-related death rates, and that in the U.S. middle and high school age children are now more likely to die as the result of a firearm injury than from any other single cause of death; that according to a report from the US Secret Service, in incidents of gun violence on school grounds 76% of attackers acquired a firearm from the home of a parent or another close relative; that every year roughly 350 children under the age of 18 unintentionally shoot themselves or someone else; that nearly 22,000 Americans die by firearm suicide every year, including over 950 children and teens; that research indicates 47% of firearm owners who have children living in their homes do not safely store at least one of their weapons; that secure firearm storage is an essential component of any effective strategy to keep the community safe; and that keeping students, teachers and staff safe from gun violence should be the responsibility of all adult stakeholders within the district.

The resolved clauses direct the Superintendent to periodically communicate the importance of safe firearm storage and other firearm safety and violence prevention measures during gun violence awareness month, and to disseminate material on an annual basis stressing the importance of secure storage of firearms by including it in the District's annual notification materials. A further clause commits the Board and Superintendent to continue working with local law enforcement agencies, medical and mental health agencies, and non-profit organizations to collaborate and increase efforts to inform District parents of their obligations regarding secure storage of firearms in their homes as well as other gun violence prevention safety measures. A final clause states the resolution shall not be construed to conflict with any existing Michigan or federal law. The vote was 7 yes, 0 no, and the resolution was declared adopted.

Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, certified that the resolution was duly adopted at a regular meeting held on the 20th day of June, 2024, and that the meeting was conducted and public notice given pursuant to and in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Sources footnoted in the resolution include news.umich.edu (firearms as top cause of death among children and adolescents), labblog.uofmhealth.org, the US Secret Service report "Protecting America's Schools," everytownresearch.org (the "Not an Accident" map and a report on the rise of firearm suicide among young Americans), a Pew Research Center guns report, and David C. Grossman et al., "Gun Storage Practices and Risk of Youth Suicide and Unintentional Firearm Injuries," JAMA 293, no. 6 (2005): 707-14.

**Additions & Deletions:** None. **Public Communication (Agenda Items):** None.

**General — Consent Agenda.** Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I on the consent agenda: minutes of the May 7, 2024 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the May 7, 2024 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the May 7, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the May 21, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report — April 2024; Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Membership Resolution 2024/2025; the 2023/2024 Budget Amendment; the 2024/2025 Budget Appropriations Resolution; and Approval of Committee for Instructional Minutes. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Personnel — Administrative Appointment, Special Education Supervisor.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Hauff that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Trevor Harker, who will begin his duties as Special Education Supervisor effective July 1, 2024. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Personnel — Assistant Superintendent, Business Services.** Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Daniel Trudel, who will begin his duties as Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, effective July 1, 2024. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Personnel — TEA Contract Ratification.** A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA (TEA) was reached on June 10, 2024. The TEA membership voted to ratify the agreement on June 19, 2024. The tentative agreement is a contract for the period February 1, 2024 through April 15, 2027, and the draft successor collective bargaining agreement with all modifications was attached for the Board's consideration. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board ratify and adopt the tentative agreement reached on June 10, 2024 for the period February 1, 2024 through April 15, 2027. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Curriculum:** None.

**Business — Serving Lines for Boulan, Larson and Wass Elementary School.** Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic that the purchase of serving lines be awarded to Stafford-Smith, Inc. in the amount of $317,179.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Business — UNOX Ovens for IAE, Larson and Smith Middle School.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the purchase of three UNOX ovens be awarded to Gold Star Products in the amount of $90,589.75 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund. Vote: 7 yes, 0 no.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items).** Mr. Walt Storrs, Troy resident, addressed the Board about flooding and poor drainage in the Sylvan Glen subdivision when the Troy Preschool was built; he had met with the City Engineer and requested to sit down with an engineer working on the new Smith Middle School regarding the issue. Alex Karpowitsch, Troy resident, addressed the Board about key performance indicators and provided Board members with copies of a PowerPoint from Detroit Public Schools titled Project 2026 Blueprint showing achievement data. Mrs. Tracy Owens, Troy resident, addressed the Board about special education in the District and informed them that her three children will not be attending Troy Schools next year.

**Other.** No other business items were listed. Board members shared sentiments about the end of the school year and wished everyone a wonderful summer. Dr. Machesky mentioned that several Board members were recognized by the Oakland County School Board Association for their achievements: he congratulated Nancy Philippart for 16 years of service on the Board, Karl Schmidt for serving 12 years on the Board, Emina Alic and Matt Haupt for becoming certified Board members receiving the Award of Merit, Vital Anne for receiving the Master Board of Education Member Award, and the entire Board for receiving the Standard of Excellence Award. He also acknowledged the entire bargaining team for their continued work in coming to an agreement. Mr. Schmidt talked about end of year celebrations and graduations, then spoke about legislative issues, the lack of funding for public schools in the governor's proposed budget, and how hard the MEA is working to get funds for public education. He announced the next Board meeting would be held on July 16th at Central Office at 9:30 in the morning.

**Adjournment.** The meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m. Respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.
